subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should this issue remain the canonical follow-up for artifact-gated status and no-idle-after-green behavior after the broader run-lifecycle reliability work landed?
rationale: Current main covers adjacent liveness and recovery failures, but this issue asks for new user-visible status policy, thresholds, telemetry, and durable state semantics that require maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Adopt as a narrow follow-up
options.body: Keep this issue open for a staged design that defines artifacts, blocker escalation, post-green completion behavior, and SQLite-backed guard state on top of the current runtime paths.

options.title: Declare lifecycle work sufficient
options.body: Close this issue if maintainers decide https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102160 intentionally covers enough of the anti-drift problem and no artifact-gated status contract should be added.

options.title: Defer policy enforcement
options.body: Leave current liveness/progress behavior as-is and document that strict artifact-gated status is not planned until more production evidence appears.

recommendation.title: Adopt as a narrow follow-up
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a staged design that defines artifacts, blocker escalation, post-green completion behavior, and SQLite-backed guard state on top of the current runtime paths.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus authored and merged the overlapping lifecycle design and is the clearest owner for deciding whether this remaining status-policy layer should exist.
